eval.title: Vale Stock Analysis 2025 (Iron ore supply & demand outlook)

call.headline_quote: So val yes it is cheaper but still not cheap enough for an absolute value investment purchase.

base_metric.name: fcf_per_share
base_metric.quote: if iron ore price are at 90 for an 8% yield the stock price if it is around 10 should be around five for a 20% yield

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: So the free cash flow year for Valet is not bad at 8%.

scenarios.name: best
scenarios.quote: if prices go above 100 then we are talking about 20% free cash flow yields which is something remarkable

scenarios.name: worst
scenarios.quote: if prices go to 80, the free cash flow goes down to 3%.

what_is_priced_in.quote: This is what they speak about. But why don't they tell me how it would look like at 60?

reasons.claim: Free cash flow yield swings enormously with iron ore price, so the stock is not cheap enough yet at current prices.
reasons.quote: in all it looks cheap but I would argue not yet cheap enough because you want to buy it when the potential free cash flow

reasons.claim: Long-term iron ore price outlook of $75-80 based on rising supply and weaker Chinese demand implies much lower cash flow yields than today.
reasons.quote: If we look at the iron or price outlook, you see that it is expected to be around 7580.

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: expected iron ore price

reasons.claim: Low-cost peers and Vale itself are ramping up production, meaning supply is more likely to exceed demand than the miner narrative of a supply gap suggests.
reasons.quote: Everyone can produce iron ore at very very low cash costs. Add the shipping at this and that. And you are at 40 likely $50 per ton.

data_check.gap_note: he says 50, as-of 4.953e+09 (FY2024); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Vale is increasing debt to pay for dam-disaster restructuring at a time when it was making a lot of money, adding risk.
reasons.quote: So they are increasing the debt in a great time where they made a lot of money which then increases a little bit the risk.

data_check.gap_note: trajectory visible at T0; no number stated

reasons.claim: Vale's free cash flow yield is better than BHP's, and its dividend yield is also better, making it relatively more attractive among iron ore miners.
reasons.quote: The free cash flow yield is much lower than Valet.

external_facts_used: Goldman Sachs prediction that iron ore demand will be stable but supply may decline slightly below demand
Vale's copper production growth target toward 700,000 tons per year
20-year iron ore price average / cycle history showing booms followed by five years of weak prices
China's transition toward a service economy reducing iron ore demand growth

critic.notes: He says Vale 'looks cheap but not yet cheap enough' (~$7-8 vs ~$10), and allows starting a position if you accept the cycle and doubling down lower — a positive wait-for-better-price/watch, i.e. fair_hold, not avoid.
